name: Siemens
summary: Siemens is a technology company working in industrial automation and software, smart infrastructure and mobility. Its careers site describes applying online and then being invited to interview, and its Siemens Graduate Program uses CV screening, an initial interview and an assessment centre, with some variation by country. Candidates commonly report technical interviews on their engineering discipline and projects, plus a behavioural or HR conversation.
rounds: Online test or recorded video interview for some roles and graduate schemes
Technical interview on your discipline, projects and problem solving
Behavioural or HR interview on motivation, teamwork and fit
Assessment centre for graduate programmes, with several exercises
looks_for: Solid fundamentals in your field: electrical, mechanical, software or automation
A practical, structured approach to solving problems
Responsibility for safety, quality and ethical conduct
Understanding of why the technology matters to the customer
Working well in diverse, international teams

questions.text: Tell me about a technical problem you solved in a project, lab or internship. How did you find the cause?
covers: The problem and what made it hard
The steps you took to narrow it down: tests, measurements, data
The fix and how you confirmed it worked

questions.text: Tell me about a time you noticed a quality or safety risk. What did you do?
covers: What you noticed and why it mattered
Who you told and how you made the case
What changed as a result

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked in a team with people from different disciplines or backgrounds.
covers: The team, the goal and your role
A difference in approach and how you bridged it
What the team delivered and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new tool or technology quickly.
covers: Why you needed it and how little time you had
How you learned it
What you delivered with it

questions.text: What's a weakness you're working on, and how are you improving it?
covers: A real weakness that matters at work, not a disguised strength
An example of when it showed
Concrete steps you're taking and progress so far

questions.text: Explain what a PLC does in a factory, and how it differs from an ordinary computer.
covers: Reading inputs from sensors and controlling outputs such as motors and valves
Built for harsh conditions and reliable real-time cycles
A simple example, such as a conveyor that stops when a sensor trips

questions.text: What is a digital twin, and how could a manufacturer use one?
covers: A virtual model of a product, machine or plant, kept up to date with real data
Uses: testing changes before making them, predicting failures, saving energy
What it needs: good data, sensors and a model you can trust

questions.text: A production line keeps stopping at the same station. How would you find out why?
covers: Gathering data: when it stops, error codes, shifts, recent changes
Checking the station's mechanics, sensors, controls and materials
Fixing the root cause and checking it stays fixed

questions.text: How would you reduce the energy a large building uses, with sensors and controls?
covers: Measuring first: where energy goes and when
Controls for heating, cooling and lighting based on occupancy and schedules
Estimating savings and checking them after the change

questions.text: Explain how a three-phase induction motor works, as you would to a first-year student.
covers: A rotating magnetic field created by three-phase current in the stator
Current induced in the rotor, which follows the field a little slower (slip)
Why industry uses them, and how speed is controlled with a drive

questions.text: Walk me through your final-year project: the goal, your design choices and the results.
covers: The goal and why you chose it
Your design choices and the alternatives you rejected
Results, limits and what you'd improve

questions.text: Why Siemens, and which of its businesses interests you most?
covers: Something specific about Siemens' technology or customers
The business you chose and how your skills fit
What you'd like to learn there

questions.text: Siemens works on digitalisation and sustainability. Which of these interests you most for your career, and why?
covers: One theme, with a concrete example from industry
How it connects to your studies or work
What you'd like to contribute

questions.text: Are you open to working on customer sites or travelling for projects?
covers: An honest answer about what you can do
Why site work helps you learn
Any limits, stated clearly and positively

tips: Revise the core of your discipline; technical interviewers commonly go back to fundamentals from your degree.
Know one or two Siemens businesses relevant to your field and the problems they solve for customers.
Siemens' careers site welcomes AI for preparing, but not during live interviews or assessments; practise answering on your own.
For a graduate assessment centre, expect several exercises as well as interviews, and treat each as a fresh start.
